name: Gautam Adani
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2008-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026); Hurun India (2015-2022); Wikidata (2023)
forbes_bio: Gautam Adani is chairman of the Ahmedabad-headquartered Adani Group, with interests in ports, airports, power generation and transmission, and green energy, among others.
The Adani Group, which began in 1988 as a commodities trading firm, expanded through acquisitions and with the support of Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi.
Adani is India's biggest airport operator and also controls Mundra Port, India's largest, in his home state of Gujarat.
In January 2023, U.S. firm Hindenburg Research accused Adani and his companies of financial fraud and stock market manipulation. The Adani Group denied any wrongdoing.
In 2026, Adani announced plans to invest $100 billion in building AI data centres across the country that will be powered by green energy.
forbes_facts: Adani owns Abbot Point, a controversial coal mining project in Australia, whose Carmichael coal mine is billed as one of the world's largest.
Adani became India's second-largest cement producer in 2022, after acquiring Swiss firm Holcim's Indian assets for $10.5 billion.
Adani says he wants to be the world's largest producer of green energy and will invest up to $70 billion on renewable energy projects.
A high school dropout, Adani spurned his father's textile shop to start his own commodities trading firm.
Adani group's shares, which had plummeted following the Hindenburg report, recovered substantially after India's Supreme Court ruled in the group's favour.

name: Chen Jianhua
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2011-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026); Hurun China (2005-2026)
forbes_bio: Chen Jianhua is the chairman of Hengli Group, one of China's largest petrochemical businesses that also has interests in tourism and property development.
Chen's wife Fan Hongwei, also a billionaire, is the chairman of the group's listed arm Hengli Petrochemical.
Born into an impoverished family, Chen quit school at the age of 13.
He later made his fortune trading textiles and acquired a state-owned chemical fiber factory before expanding into petrochemicals.
The couple's son, Chen Hanlun, is a director and general manager of Guangdong Songfa Ceramics. Their daughter, Chen Yiting, is Hengli Group's vice president.

name: Antonia Ax:son Johnson
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2017-2025); Hurun Global (2015-2026)
forbes_bio: Antonia Ax:son Johnson is the fourth generation member of her family to own conglomerate Axel Johnson.
Ax:son Johnson succeeded her father as head of the privately held, diversified trading company in 1982.
She stepped down as chairman in March 2015 and handed the reins over to her daughter, Caroline Berg.
She still has a seat on the board, and most of the ownership.
Founded by her great-grandfather in 1873, the conglomerate now has interests in energy, real estate, industrial products and grocery store chains.
It also holds a 50% stake in Axfood AB, one of the largest food companies in Scandinavia.
forbes_facts: Ax:son Johnson went to Radcliffe College in Cambridge, MA as an exchange student in the early 1960s.
Ax:son Johnson is an avid equestrian and breeder, and is the owner of Olympics-competing horses.

name: Jay Chaudhry
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2020-2025); Hurun Global (2020-2026); Hurun India (2019-2022); Wikidata (2025); SEC insider holdings (2026)
forbes_bio: Jay Chaudhry is CEO of Zscaler, a cybersecurity firm he founded in 2008. It went public in March 2018.
He and his family own around 35% of the Nasdaq-listed firm.
Before Zscaler, Chaudhry founded four other tech companies that were all acquired: SecureIT, CoreHarbor, CipherTrust and AirDefense.
In 1996, Chaudhry and his wife, Jyoti, both quit their jobs and used their life savings to start cybersecurity firm SecureIT, his first startup.
His hometown, a village in the Himalayas in India, did not have electricity or running water until he was in the 8th and 10th grade, respectively.
Chaudhry moved to the U.S. in 1980 to attend graduate school and now lives in Nevada, after relocating from the Bay Area.
forbes_facts: Chaudhry's first time on a plane was his flight to the U.S. in 1980, after he was admitted to an engineering and management masters program at U. of Cincinnati.

name: Viktor Rashnikov
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2005-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026)
forbes_bio: Viktor Rashnikov is the majority owner of Magnitogorsk Iron & Steel Works (MMK).
Rashnikov got his start as a mechanic at MMK back in 1967.
He built his ownership in the company to nearly 100% by buying shares on the market.
Rashnikov stepped down as CEO of MMK in 2011 after 14 years in the job. He was sanctioned by the EU and U.K. in March 2022.
His youngest daughter, Olga, joined the board and the strategic planning committee in 2012. She resigned from the board in March 2022.
In February 2022 Rashnikov transferred his shares of MMK from a Cyprus-registered company to Russian Altair LLC.
In November 2022 he received the award Hero of Labour of the Russian Federation from Vladimir Putin "for special labor service for the country and people".
forbes_facts: Rashnikov was associated with a 460-foot, $240 million (estimated value) yacht named "Ocean Victory" but its ultimate ownership is currently unclear.
A passionate hockey fan, Rashnikov has been president of hockey club Metallurg Magnitogorsk since 1999.

name: Taylor Thomson
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2025); Hurun Global (2022-2026)
forbes_bio: Taylor Thomson is one of six billionaire heirs to the media and publishing empire founded by her grandfather Roy Thomson (d. 1976).
The family's biggest holding: more than 310 million shares of Thomson Reuters.
Thomson owns around 14% of the business through the family's investment firm, Woodbridge.
The family's other assets include the Toronto-based Globe and Mail newspaper, and the Montreal Canadiens and Winnipeg Jets sports teams.

name: Philip Ng
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes real-time (former) (2023); Forbes annual (2013-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026)
forbes_bio: Philip Ng and his brother Robert control Far East Organization, Singapore's largest private landlord and property developer.
The group was founded by their father Ng Teng Fong, who moved from China to Singapore in 1934 and came to be known as "The King of Orchard Road."
Their Hong Kong arm, Sino Group, is run by older sibling Robert and his son Daryl, while Philip oversees the Singapore interests.
Singapore-listed Far East Orchard repurposed the century-old former Westminster Fire Station in London into a luxury development with 17 apartments and put it on sale in 2022.
forbes_facts: The brothers are staunch Christians and refer to Far East as a Christian enterprise.
Founder Ng Teng Fong spurned his family's grocery store and got into real estate in 1960 against his father's wishes.

name: Miguel Krigsner
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2014-2025); Hurun Global (2018-2026)
forbes_bio: Bolivian-born Miguel Krigsner founded Grupo Boticario, Brazil's second-largest cosmetics company behind number one, Natura.
Grupo Boticario operates in more than 50 countries; Krigsner individually owns approximately 80% of the business.
His brother-in-law Artur Grynbaum joined as a financial assistant and worked his way up to president of the group by 2008. He owns about 20% of the group.
In 1990 Krigsner created the Boticario Group Foundation dedicated to environmental protection, which receives about 1% of Grupo Boticario's net income annually.
Today, Krigsner and Grynbaum serve as president and vice president, respectively, of the Grupo Boticario advisory board.
forbes_facts: His parents fled Nazi Germany to settle in Bolivia in the 1940s. Krigsner was born in Bolivia and moved to Brazil in 1961.

name: Peter Kellogg
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2001-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026); Wikidata (2025)
forbes_bio: Peter Kellogg sold brokerage house Spear, Leeds & Kellogg to Goldman Sachs for $6.5 billion in cash and stock in 2000.
Kellogg joined the firm, where his father was a partner, in 1973 and took over several years later.
Under his leadership, the firm became the first specialist brokerage to control more than 10% of the stocks trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
After selling to Goldman in 2000, Kellogg turned his attention to reinsurance outfit IAT, which he led as CEO until 2015 and still chairs.
Kellogg has donated more than $4 million to the U.S. ski and snowboarding teams.

name: Ratmir Timashev
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026)
forbes_bio: Ratmir Timashev is the cofounder and former CEO of Columbus, Ohio-based data management firm Veeam.
He and his college friend Andrei Baronov cofounded Veeam in 2006 and sold it to VC firm Insight Partners for $5 billion in 2020.
Before Veeam, Timashev and Baronov cofounded systems management tools outfit Aelita Software in 1996; they sold it to Quest Software for $115 million in 2004.
In 2026, Timashev launched Oh.io, a VC firm that's aiming to invest $100 million to bring 100 early-stage startups to Columbus, Ohio over five years.
Timashev is a major donor to his alma mater, Ohio State, giving around $150 million including a $110 million gift in 2020 to establish the Center for Software Innovation.
forbes_facts: Timashev renounced his Russian citizenship in 2024 in opposition to the invasion of Ukraine and is now a dual American-Cypriot citizen.
While working as a PhD student in Moscow in the early 1990s, Timashev fixed roofs and cleaned windows in the summer and weekends to earn more money.

name: Robin Li
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2008-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2015); Wikidata (2019); Hurun Unicorn founders (2026)
forbes_bio: Robin Li is the cofounder, chairman and CEO of search engine operator Baidu, which is dual-listed on the Nasdaq and in Hong Kong.
The company counts online advertising as its bread-and-butter business. It is also expanding aggressively in AI.
Baidu in 2023 rolled out a chatbot rival to ChatGPT called Ernie.
It also operates driverless robotaxi services in mainland China, and secured trial permits for such services in Dubai and Hong Kong.
The company's semiconductor design unit, Kunlunxin, counts customers that include Chinese telecom giant China Mobile.

name: Hans Peter Wild
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2014-2025); Hurun Global (2016-2026); SEC insider holdings (2025)
forbes_bio: Hans-Peter Wild sold the last of a WILD Flavors stake to agricultural processing giant Archer-Daniels Midland in 2014 for about $3 billion in cash.
His father founded WILD Flavors in 1931 and the company grew into a leading supplier of flavors and extracts, sweeteners, and fermentation technology.
He worked for a marketer of mineral oil and chemicals before joining the family business in 1974 and helping to expand its portfolio.
Wild still owns Capri Sun, the famed fruit juice brand that originated in the 1960s.
Today Capri Sun is consumed in more than 100 countries and generates an estimated annual revenue of $500 million.
forbes_facts: As a student studying business and law, Wild traveled abroad in search of innovative alternative sources of raw materials for the family business.
His biggest marketing coup was signing Muhammad Ali, then at the peak of his boxing career, as a spokesman for Capri Sun.
